sources.summary: El País in English (14 April 2025) on the murder of trans woman Sara Millerey González Borja, 32, in Bello (Antioquia): beaten and thrown into a creek on 4 April 2025, onlookers filming instead of helping; the third killing of an LGBT+ person in Bello that year and part of 13 trans people killed nationally in Q1 2025; the case triggered vigils in several cities. National-context source, not Huila-specific.

CNN 'As Equals' investigation (6 Aug 2025), 'Viral video of her torture shocked Colombia. The killings didn't stop there': documents the continuing wave of killings of queer and trans people in Colombia after the Bello murder, and the framing that in parts of Colombia being queer means 'to sign your own death sentence'. National-context source; mostly a video/interactive feature with limited extractable body text.

The Guardian (30 July 2024), 'We are killed for what we are': trans women in Colombia targeted by armed groups — armed groups in Caquetá circulated flyers threatening a 'social cleansing' of trans women as military targets; a trans woman with a salon was given a week to leave town; more than 40 trans women killed the previous year and 41 in 2023; armed-group displacement of trans women documented. National-pattern source relevant to intercity/border travel risk, not Huila-specific.
